sub.en: Does the sentence say when it happened? That is the question to ask.

items.q: I ___ in New York for about three years now.
items.why: The period runs up to now, so the present perfect is used.

items.q: I ___ into this flat three years ago.
items.why: three years ago is a finished point, so the past simple is used.

items.q: The rent ___ three times since then.
It ___ me more than an hour to get to work today.
items.why: Here the journey itself is over, so the past simple is natural even though today is not finished.

items.q: I ___ mugged yet, but my best friend has.
items.why: yet belongs to the present perfect: up to now, it has not happened.

items.why: the past month is not finished, so the present perfect counts what has happened so far.

A period running up to now takes the present perfect.
ever … before asks about experience up to now.
RECYCLED from Lesson 13: enjoy is always followed by -ing.

tts: I’ve lived in New York for about three years now. It’s an exciting place to live, but there are quite a few annoying things about it too.
For a start, it’s incredibly expensive. When I moved into my flat three years ago, the rent was already quite high, but it has gone up three times since then.
It can also be quite a violent place. I haven’t been mugged yet, but my best friend has. Luckily she wasn’t actually hurt; they just took her bag.
And the traffic is dreadful. It took me more than an hour to get to work today, and nearly as long to get home.

However, I’ve never lived anywhere where there is so much to do. Over the past month I’ve been to the theatre three times, as well as to a number of art exhibitions. I’ve also just started salsa classes.
So, although living in New York has some bad points, on balance I don’t think I want to live anywhere else in the world.

write.q: Write about a game, a film or a series you know really well. Use the present perfect for how long you have known it and for your experience of it, and the past simple for the specific times you can date.
plan: what it is and how long
when you first met it (a date)
write.model: I’ve been playing the same football game for about six years now, which is longer than I have kept any other habit. I bought the first version in 2019, mostly because a friend at work would not stop talking about it. The game itself has changed three times since then, and honestly not all of the changes have been improvements: the last update made the menus almost inaccessible on a hand-held screen. I have never played it online, because I can’t stand losing to strangers at midnight. On balance, though, I’d still recommend it. I played it last night for two hours and I did not once look at my phone.

speak.q: Describe it out loud in about a minute. Be careful to switch: present perfect when you do not say when, past simple when you do.
